summary: legal checked in 5 executive handoff item(s)

items.summary: Risk disposition: blocked for public launch, monetization expansion, alert expansion, and security-sensitive release. Conditional for bounded reversible growth that adds no credentials, permissions, dependencies, new data collection, or cross-site behavior and preserves consent, disclosures, provenance, claims, copyright/trademark, affiliate, platform-policy, and age-sensitive boundaries. Evidence: Woot documentation establishes API access but not rights to store, derive, cache, publicly display, alert on, or monetize deal and price-history data; current terms restrict those uses. All four launch-readiness tasks remain open. Security, accuracy/freshness, measurement, and owner gates are incomplete. Exact decision: keep SearchWoot private, preview-only, and unlaunched; keep rights outreach unsent pending human-counsel review and owner authorization. Next evidence action: attach and review one consolidated read-only bundle covering field-level rights, deployed data flow and retention, log/vendor/incident procedures, consent and GA4 configuration, accuracy/freshness controls, and rollback evidence.

Launch-readiness tracking is active: 0 of 4 tasks closed and 4 remain open. No task is closed because direct evidence is missing for source rights, field-level permissions, retention, deletion/correction/access, notification consent, GA4 settings, vendor coverage, incident procedures, accuracy/freshness controls, and rollback. Continue read-only evidence work only; do not close tasks without direct evidence.

Data-use review: Woot API deal and price-history data is blocked. Missing written permission or an API agreement plus field-level limits for fetch, storage, derivatives, caching, display, alerts, attribution, freshness, correction, takedown, trademarks, images, prices, affiliate use, and advertising. Smallest next action: complete the internal counsel packet and obtain human-counsel review. User alert rules and sync results are evidence_needed; missing data inventory, identifiers, retention, deletion/correction/access, processor terms, notification consent, and unsubscribe behavior. Smallest next action: produce a read-only deployed/repository data-flow and retention table. GA4 analytics is evidence_needed; missing deployed consent and withdrawal behavior, GA4 property/data-sharing settings, retention settings, and jurisdictional review. Smallest next action: capture consent and GA4 configuration evidence without enabling new tracking. Operational logs and Cloudflare hosting data are evidence_needed; missing log-field inventory, retention/access controls, vendor terms or DPA coverage, incident handling, and request procedures. Smallest next action: produce a read-only log/vendor/incident/request inventory.

Fleet compliance disposition: technical compliance baseline is not certification; 35 sites pass, 18 fail, and 6 are unknown, with open banner, consent, GA4, privacy, and terms findings. Analytics quality is yellow and unavailable sources must not be treated as zero. Revenue evidence is limited to 6,219 clicks, 28 ordered items, 6 shipped items, and $4.92 aggregate Amazon commission for 2026-09-21; it is not site-attributable. Do not block ordinary growth solely for incomplete telemetry, but do not make unsupported revenue, ROI, attribution, or causal-lift claims. Keep private or gated properties private until concrete launch evidence exists.

Private-site decision: keep complicated.work, deadlymaracas.com, and driveford.net parked, private, preview-only, and unlaunched. Missing evidence includes dated ownership, preview/build validation, compliance baseline, security controls, measurement boundaries, rollback points, and explicit blockers; execution-owner prerequisites are also unresolved. No publish, deployment, DNS change, analytics configuration, monetization, spending, dependency addition, or queue entry is cleared. Next evidence action: attach a dated readiness packet for each property.
